extracted.intended_audience: California state agency staff and rule drafters submitting regulations to OAL
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the California Office of Administrative Law's regular rulemaking process under the Administrative Procedure Act, including when it applies and core procedural requirements for adopting regulations. Focused on ensuring public notice/comment, availability of supporting documents, and creating an adequate rulemaking record for OAL and court review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of the regular rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: The vast majority of regulations adopted pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) are submitted to OAL as 'regular' rulemakings; unless a proposed rulemaking action is submitted to OAL as an 'emergency' rulemaking or is exempted from the APA, the regular rulemaking process must be complied with when an agency undergoes a rulemaking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines whether the regular process applies: follow the regular rulemaking procedures unless the action is properly classified and submitted as an emergency rulemaking or the action is statutorily/exemptly outside the APA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive public notice and comment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The regular rulemaking process includes comprehensive public notice and comment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide adequate public notice and opportunities for public comment as part of the regular process; this is a central procedural requirement intended to facilitate participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of supporting documents and information
rubrics_metrics.description: The regular rulemaking process requires that documents and information on which the rulemaking action is based are available for review and inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must make underlying documents and information accessible to the public to support transparency and enable meaningful comment; ensure records are organized and available for inspection per OAL expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an adequate rulemaking record for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The comprehensive process is intended to further the goal of public participation in the rulemaking process and to create an adequate rulemaking record for review by OAL and the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking should produce a complete administrative record (including notices, comments, supporting analyses, and responses) sufficient for OAL and judicial review; prioritize documentation that demonstrates how input and evidence informed regulatory decisions.
